actions.added_meaning: Selected exact House 20011 DOD border-support funding and authority boundaries follow. House 20011 DOD border-support appropriation: In addition to amounts otherwise available, there are appropriated to the Secretary of Defense for fiscal year 2025, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, to remain available until September 30, 2029, $5,000,000,000 for activities in support of border operations, including deployment of military personnel, operations and maintenance, counter-narcotics and counter- transnational criminal organization mission support, the operation of and construction in national defense areas, the temporary detention of migrants on Department of Defense installations. Both exact provisions are additional fiscal year 2025 appropriations to the Secretary of Defense available until September 30, 2029, not DHS/ICE/CBP funds or evidence of actual spending, deployment, detention, removal, conditions or outcomes. Own border operations, military personnel, operations/maintenance, counter-narcotics/transnational criminal organization support, national-defense-area operation/construction and temporary migrant detention on DOD installations purposes are retained. No status/crime/detention-duration/child/family condition is invented from other DHS/ICE grants or from the parent package. Funding a stated activity does not by itself resolve which military/civilian actor may exercise each power or establish a universal arrest/search/detention authorization. Whole original chapter 15 operative sections 271-284 are bound, with civilian-request, applicable-law, jurisdiction, support-type, geography, approval, military-readiness, reimbursement, notice/report and agency/definition conditions. They are not all simultaneously universal duties: 277(b) has its own National Guard support boundary; 282/283 have emergency/DOJ/approval conditions; 284 has its own additional-authority/exception/limited-waiver rules. Section 275 retains regulation duty, named Army/Navy/Air Force/Marine Corps members, direct search/seizure/arrest/similar activity restriction and unless otherwise authorized by law. Section 276 preparedness condition is retained with the actual 284(e) short-term adverse-effect/two-determination waiver and 284(g) relationship; no absolute no-adverse-effect summary or universal waiver. Section 278 preserves prior executive authority rather than granting an unlimited new enforcement power. Full 284 retains authorized requestors, domestic/foreign and 25-mile conditions, drug-corridor construction, notice/reports and definitions; no general migrant-detainment or all-border-construction authority inferred from the chapter heading. Original numerical legacy references in 273/274/279/282/283 remain as printed, without silent repair or interpretation by title alone. Proposed national-defense-area/temporary-detention/direct-participation and support-path application is reserved as question 61, with all relevant lawful-authority conditions, rather than accepted or declared categorically unlawful. Other H.R.1 components and separately reserved questions remain unfinished. House appropriates $5 billion and uses its own including list. It does not print the Senate in-accordance-with-chapter 15 phrase, but that absence is not represented as an exemption from underlying law or unlimited military enforcement power. Chapter15 is source-grounded legal context for reserved application, not a Senate clause copied into House operative text. Served EH comparison retains exact separate bytes; adopted June correction witnesses have no direct 20011 amendment, no whole-EH vote-time substitution.
